dusk: The lamps come on along the street.
Dusk. Somebody is frying onions, and the street smells of it.
The light goes gold, then blue. The street is awake.
turnedIn: You shut the book early. The street is only just lighting up.
Enough for one day. There is still a little evening left.

out-of-time: The sand has run out. That was the evening.
The last grain drops, and not a minute wasted.
bed: You turn in. The street carries on quietly without you.
Bed. The kettle will keep until morning.
midnight-oil: You look up from the bench and the street has gone dark. The evening went by without you.
The lamp burns low over the workbench. Everybody else went to bed some time ago.

morning: Morning. The street smells of bread and wet stone.
A new day. Somewhere a goose is already complaining.
Morning, and the kettle is on.
newOrders: There are new orders on the board.
